items.title: docs: one shape for eighteen ports, a results table, and an API reference with parameters
items.body:
A full read of `docs/`, `README.md` and the generated API reference, against
what the code actually does.

## The eighteen port pages had two shapes, and eleven had no command

The seven benchmark-faithful ports opened with a blockquote and a
`Paper / Repo / Dataset / Layer` table; the eleven microports opened with a bold
fidelity line and a `Paper / Upstream / Definition / Domain` one; OpenEvolve
followed neither. The eleven had no **Run it** section at all, so eleven of
eighteen runnable examples documented no way to run them.

All eighteen now open and close identically. Five `Domain` rows named a dataset
the port had stopped using — AFlow, Self-Refine and PromptBreeder said the
arithmetic fixture and measure on GSM8K; Voyager and SkillWeaver said 12 tasks
against splits that are 48.

## The results were nowhere addable up

New: [**Measured results — all eighteen**](https://github.com/Birfy/agentdescent/blob/docs/eighteen-ports-and-api-parameters/docs/self-evolution-examples.md#measured-results-all-eighteen),
computed from `bench/results/*.json` — the eleven in one comparable block (same
runner, three seeds, 80 rollouts, 8 workers), the seven separately because their
budgets differ. Building it found **Agent0's mean gain reported as +0.458 where
all three seeds moved +0.500**.

## `docs/api.md` named every entry point and showed no parameters

`_signature` collapsed anything over 96 characters to `(...)` — 67 of them, and
exactly the wrong 67: `evolve`, `evolve_skill`, all three `evolve_*_dir`,
`openai_compatible`, `async_evolve`. The NumPy `Parameters` sections in the
docstrings were dropped whole by `_summary`, so prose that was written and tested
never reached a reader.

The generator now prints the full signature under a collapsed heading, one
parameter per line, plus a table of type / default / prose wherever the docstring
documents one. `evolve()` goes from one line to 42 documented parameters. Two
defects surfaced on the way: the keyword-only `*` marker was re-emitted before
*every* keyword-only parameter (invisible while signatures collapsed), and
`SECTIONS` declared `agentdescent.worker`, a module that does not exist. Three
tests pin the new behaviour.

## What was deleted

- **`SgdSkillAggregator`** — documented in five places, exists in none.
  `port-fidelity.md` said in one paragraph that it was removed and in the next
  that `--sgd-descent` opts into it.
- **`matrix-parallel-speedup.md`, `matrix-async.md`** — every table read `*TBD*`.
  Folded into a rewritten `matrix-overview.md` that says which columns of the
  retained run still describe something real (the timing) and which do not (the
  quality, measured on a fixture that no longer exists).
- **`self-evolution-examples.md`'s seven per-algorithm sections** — restatements
  of the dedicated pages. EvoSkill's two overlapping dataset sections.
- **`results.md`'s port table** — a stale second copy (ACE at `0.844 → 0.889`
  against the page's `0.719 → 0.766`; DGM's surrogate row against a
  real-objective one). It points at the single table now and keeps the finding
  only visible across ports: a difficulty knob calibrated on one model does not
  transfer.
- **Twelve bug post-mortems** on the port pages, eight more compressed to the
  fidelity point they contained. A fixed defect is history; the pages are
  reference.

## What was corrected

- README carried the efficiency numbers `results.md` itself records as retracted
  (`7.1x / 5.9x / 2.4x / 3.0x / 193.6s → 90.0s`, "produced by hand and could not
  be re-run"); `verifier.md` quoted the same dead `193.6s`; `efficiency.md` said
  83% where its own corrected table says 93%.
- "All eighteen `--dry-run` with zero network" — true of the seven, not of the
  eleven, which build their policy and so fetch their split first.
- `docs/evolution.md`'s knob table covered 21 parameters of 42 and gave
  `cheap_eval_tasks` a default of "all" that has been 8 for some time. It is now
  three tables — plug-in seams, the `Policies` decision plane with every field,
  and the plain settings grouped by what they control.

## Recorded rather than fixed

`standard_main` declares `--async-ratio`, `--eval-concurrency`, `--eval-cache`
and `--val-cap` and passes none of them to `run_port`, so they do nothing on all
eleven MethodPolicy ports. Every recorded row carries `async_ratio: 2`, which no
documented command can set. Choosing a default changes what an async run does, so
it is a decision rather than a docs fix — it is written up under
[the MethodPolicy command line](https://github.com/Birfy/agentdescent/blob/docs/eighteen-ports-and-api-parameters/docs/self-evolution-examples.md#the-methodpolicy-command-line).

---

`pytest` passes in full; `mkdocs build --strict` is clean and every internal
anchor resolves (`tests/test_docs_links.py`).

Audit of README, landing page and deck against `BENCHMARK.md` — which all three cite as their source.

### 1. The landing page's exposure row was wrong in all four cells

Under-reported median, p95 and max; over-reported the minimum.

| | p50 | p95 | min | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BENCHMARK.md | 13.71s | 25.55s | 9.72s | 26.71s |
| README.md | 13.71s | 25.55s | 9.72s | 26.71s ✅ |
| **index.html** | **13.38s** | **25.01s** | **10.47s** | **25.28s** ❌ |

`MAX = 25.28` sat below the tallest cycle (26.55s), so that bar rendered at **105%** and was cut off by the frame — all three slow cycles flattened against the ceiling. The landing page already used 26.71.

### 3. "Cycles 10–13 / four consecutive" survived in three more places

`README.md:764`, the deck's visible chart caption, and the bar chart's **aria-label** — so screen-reader users got the false version too. Slow is `> 20s` = cycles **1, 13, 18** (25.17s, 26.55s, 24.39s), not adjacent.

### Why CI didn't catch any of it

`proof-integrity.spec.ts` claimed to check "the published site's headline figures against BENCHMARK.md" but only asserted the response p50/p95 against the hero stat — **the results table was never read**. Now it:

- asserts every cell of both rows, scoped to the latency table by caption
- asserts no bar exceeds 100% of the chart frame

Both new tests were verified to **fail on the old values and pass on the corrected ones** before commit.

Plus: `.addr-k` was `flex:0 0 180px` while "RoachMotelSpender (drainer)" measures 192px, so it alone wrapped. 200px puts all three on one line.

items.title: Refresh results + README tables after strict-UTF-8 fixes
items.body:
Full `RUNS=5` run on freshly bootstrapped corelibs. Gate green (434 B / 494 B), all 18 targets OK.

## Why the numbers moved

sofabgen v0.18.0 brought **strict UTF-8 validation** into `corelib-cpp` and `corelib-zig` through the lockstep corelib re-clone. `languages/cpp/` was byte-identical and the regen commit message named only "Rust/Java/C#/Zig", so nothing in this repo flagged it — but it is real per-message work (6 strings, validated on both encode *and* decode) and it cost C++ 16 % and Zig 17 %.

Keeping it is what holds the comparison fair: protobuf's proto3 C++ codegen calls `VerifyUTF8` on parse and `VerifyUtf8String` on serialize **unconditionally**, with no flag to turn it off. Disabling ours would have bought throughput by skipping work protobuf pays for.

Both validators have since gained an 8-byte SWAR ASCII fast path ([corelib-cpp#42](https://github.com/sofa-buffers/corelib-cpp/pull/42), [corelib-zig#21](https://github.com/sofa-buffers/corelib-zig/pull/21)), recovering roughly a third. This run includes them.

| | before v0.18.0 | regression | **this run** |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| C++ | 324.9 | 272.3 | **303.2** |
| Zig | 548.5 | 412.1 | **487.9** |

## Prose corrected against the new numbers

Four claims would otherwise have been wrong:

- **Java is now exactly at parity** on `msg/s` (1.00×), not ahead — so *"every compiled **and JIT** language beats protobuf"* is narrowed to *"every compiled language"*.
- Zig headline 2.4× → **2.1×**
- Python 0.08× / 0.09× → **0.09× / 0.10×**
- EmbeddedProto 2.6× → **2.7×**

The bare-metal footprint range (1.32×–1.93×) was recomputed and still holds, so it is unchanged.

## Footprint

`rust-cortex-m` +20 B, `cpp-riscv` +6 B, `rust-riscv` +24 B — the strict-UTF-8 cost in the Rust/C++ embedded codecs, **byte-identical across three separate runs**. The C++ fix adds no footprint here: the cpp-embedded family builds against `corelib-c-cpp`, which did not move.

## Caveats

**Zig's absolute number is the least reliable value in the table.** It swung 412 / 455 / 488 across three full runs, and only the last carries the fix — the 412↔455 spread happened with *no* code change. The direction is backed by an interleaved A/B (455 → 480); the absolute 487.9 wants a second full run before anything leans on it.

**Two sign flips are unexplained and unrelated to UTF-8:** Go drops to 0.95× MB/s (was 1.03×) and typescript-bun lands at 0.99× msg/s. `corelib-go` did not move during the bootstrap. I took the numbers as measured rather than explaining them away.

items.title: Fix two wrong numbers in the fly's-eye results table, verified against the book
items.body:
The example's conclusion was right and the table underneath it was not. Two of
the three rows said something a biologist should have distrusted, and one of them
contradicted the very book the example reproduces.

## The homeodomain was reported at 60%. It is 90%

`conserved_blocks` returns the ungapped segments of **one** Smith–Waterman
alignment. BLAST reports **HSPs** — separate local alignments, each with its own
E-value. Treating those as the same thing glued the homeodomain to its flanks:

| PAX6 region | aligned | identity |
|---|---|---|
| paired domain 4–136 | 132 | **94%** |
| **homeodomain 208–267** | 60 | **90%** |
| flank before, 182–207 | 26 | 46% |
| flank after, 268–327 | 60 | 35% |

The block containing the homeodomain runs 182–327 and reports the average, 60%,
over a span 2.4× longer than the domain — describing one of the most conserved
DNA-binding motifs known as barely above average.

`identity_over()` answers that narrower question separately. `discover.py` now
prints both: the blocks the alignment found unaided, **and** the identity inside
each annotated domain. The discovery still leans on nothing but the alignment;
`label()` says "contains the X" when that is what is true.

## The third block was not a linker. It was noise

19% identity over 32 residues was presented as *"linker, far freer to mutate"* —
a functional reading it never earned. Align eyeless against **shuffled** PAX6 and
the aligner still produces blocks, because that is what a local aligner does: it
extends while the score stays positive.

```
  real block len=133 id=93.2%  ->  0/74 shuffled blocks match it   signal
  real block len=146 id=59.6%  ->  0/74 shuffled blocks match it   signal
  real block len= 32 id=18.8%  -> 68/74 shuffled blocks match it   NOISE
```

Worse than average noise (the null averages 25.6%). `block_identity_null()` and
`above_noise()` make that a computed verdict rather than an eyeball — and the
honest version of the lesson is the stronger one: where evolution was not
watching, the result is indistinguishable from a shuffle.

## And a denominator

*"217 of 311 aligned residues are IDENTICAL"* summed only blocks ≥ 20 aa, which
is 80% of the alignment. `alignment_totals()` reports the whole thing —
253/389, 65% — and both figures now print with their own denominators.

## Verified against the source

Checking the 2001 O'Reilly title the example reproduces settled three things:

- **It confirmed the numbers.** Human protein: the 447 aa PIR entry `A41644`.
  Region 1: 24–169 / 17–161, 128/146 (87%), 256 bits, E = 5e-67. Region 2:
  398–477 / 222–301, 68/80 (85%), 142 bits, E = 1e-32. All now in the README as
  a table rather than one half-remembered coordinate.
- **It corrected this repo.** An earlier draft claimed the book "ran BLASTP: SEG
  low-complexity filtering, X-drop extension". The book states none of that.
  Those were the era's defaults, but asserting them as if the source said so is
  the same over-claiming the rest of this example was just cleaned of. Reduced to
  what is verifiable.
- **It closed an open question better than expected.** The README had said the
  eyeless entry could not be identified offline. The real answer: **the book
  never names it** — the figure shows an unlabelled `Query`. Nothing to look up,
  so nothing invented. And the coordinate shift is not a constant offset
  (24 → 57 at one end, 398 → 402 at the other), so the sequences differ by
  internal indels, not a longer N-terminus.

**The book also supplies the evidence for the first fix.** Its region 2 is
**80 residues at 85%**, bracketing the homeodomain. Ours over the same biology
was 146 residues at 60%. The book, the UniProt annotation and `identity_over()`
all agree on ~90%; only the raw block disagreed, and the raw block was the thing
that should never have carried the domain's name.

## Also

`Drosophila` has two Pax6 paralogues — `eyeless` and `twin of eyeless`, with
`toy` upstream of `ey` — plus the more distant `eyegone`. "The fly's Pax6 gene"
is a convenience, and the duplication is now noted.

## Verification

Example tests 10 → 16, three of them pinning the defects directly. Repo suite
305, `ruff`, `ruff format` and `mypy nanoloop/` clean. Both commits green in
isolation.

## Deleted (fully shipped)

- **`angular-21-upgrade.md`** — its own status line read *"kept as the reusable reference"*, verbatim the thing the policy forbids. Angular is on 21.2.17, and both "optional" follow-ups (the ProxyZone shim, migrating `fakeAsync` specs) shipped with the zoneless flip — `zone.js` is gone from the polyfills and from `package.json`. ## Pruned to what is owed

- **`scalability.md`** — S3's Train-side windowing shipped end to end and the two Find endpoints are built; the item now states the remaining Find-flow work (with the atomicity requirement and the Diversity-probe regression the window introduced on the Train side too) instead of a fix sketch for code that exists.
- **`vtsbrowse-empirical-tuning.md`** — Part 1 is done and its defaults are in `vtscore/config.py`; the Results tables duplicated the HTML report. What remains is the pyramid sweep, the browser-required canvas review, and the `compact_layout` rework the sweep implied.
- **`max-patch-experiment.md`** and **`population-anchored-calibration.md`** — dropped the completed-study narrative and the "DONE —" item respectively.

Two of the three unreferenced reports turned out to bear directly on an open plan item, and they reorder its roadmap:

- The **OpenLogo** study (27k unstaged photos) measured Stage-1 VLAD recall at 2.5% and located the loss at **descriptor matching** — 65% of true pairs die before RANSAC runs. The study also contradicts the plan's *"jump straight to homography"* non-goal outright (8-DoF is strictly worse; 6-DoF buys 2.3 pt of recall for 5.6× the false verifications), and caught a **deterministic 30th-vote transient** in the shared MLP trainer — recorded as a live bug.
- The **screenshot/scan** study is even more direct: SIFT verifies 5.1% of true scanned-doc pairs against SuperPoint+LightGlue's 41%, and SP+LG beats SigLIP on both document corpora — the first time structural search wins on a real corpus. `vtscore/media/structural_splg.py` and `structural_geometry.py` are already in the tree with nothing consuming them, so the plan now names the three integration items that block wiring them up (fp16 descriptor persistence, its own inlier floor ≈24, deps/GPU gating), plus the 3-DoF and 224 px-tiling findings.

Telegram and Email shipped with adapters, tests and wizard entries; six pages still said three platforms. `MCP_FEATURES.md` still claimed server mode was "not part of this first integration" long after `--mcp-serve` landed.

The old "Known documentation drift" table is gone — all three of its claims about `README.md` were themselves stale. In its place are the commands to re-derive each count, so the next drift is self-correcting.

## 3. Shipped guardrails documented as missing

`11-architecture.md` listed under "Known architectural gaps":

- **"No audit trail"** — `audit_log` writes one redacted JSON line per gated decision at mode `0600`
- **"No token/cost accounting"** — `max_turn_cost_usd` bounds a turn's spend

Both exist. A reader deciding whether this is safe to deploy would have concluded it keeps no record of what ran. Corrected to the gap that is actually real: nothing aggregates spend *across* runs, and nothing reads `model_telemetry` back.

## 4. Structure

Navigation is now grouped **Start here → Guides → Reference → Development**, in both the wiki index and the generated sidebar, so looking something up does not mean walking a flat numbered list.

**Filenames are deliberately unchanged.** `sync_wiki.py` maps source files to published page names, so regrouping alters no wiki URL. Renaming the sources would have broken every existing link for no reader benefit.

New: [15-faq.md](docs/wiki/15-faq.md). Troubleshooting covers symptoms but not the questions people actually arrive with — why did it refuse that, how do I turn a tool off, can a web page instruct my agent.

`build_sidebar()` now fails loudly if a page in `PAGES` is not assigned to a section. It previously looped over `PAGES` and so could not omit a page; explicit sections make that failure possible, hence the guard.

## 5. Suite results removed from the docs

[12-testing-and-verification.md](docs/wiki/12-testing-and-verification.md) carried a results table (`627 tests, 0 failed`). Tallies go stale the moment anyone adds a test, and a red result caused by a missing local prerequisite reads as broken code when it is nothing of the kind.

Removed the counts, the results table and the failure discussion. Added a **Prerequisites** section instead: install the sandbox runtime first, because Agent8088 refuses to run commands without isolation. Results belong in a CI run, not in a page a reader has to trust.

## 6. Provider key precedence — settled, not deferred

An earlier draft of this PR said this was still `xfail`. **That was wrong.** It has already been reconciled in the code:

- no `xfail` remains in `tests/test_providers.py`
- the docstring and the tests now agree
- all seven precedence tests pass

Order is `.env` key store → explicit `api_key` in `config.txt` → `os.environ` (ambient last, so a stray shell export cannot redirect a configured provider).

Both wiki pages already documented exactly this, so no doc change was needed. But `.claude/skills/project-conventions/SKILL.md` still described it as an open disagreement, which would have sent the next reader chasing a conflict that no longer exists — corrected there.

## 7. Comparative references removed

Several pages explained a design choice by pointing at how another project does it. Those now stand on their own, so a reader does not need outside context to follow the reasoning:

- [03-permissions-and-security.md](docs/wiki/03-permissions-and-security.md) — "why there is no separate approval mode" now states the argument directly: a second setting that can wave a gate through contradicts `permission_mode`, and an LLM judging another LLM's output can be talked out of its judgement by the same injected content it is meant to catch.
- [03-permissions-and-security.md](docs/wiki/03-permissions-and-security.md) — the unattended-runs note now explains why `AGENT8088_UNATTENDED` is frozen at import: a per-call read would let anything inside the process flip it mid-turn.
- [02-configuration.md](docs/wiki/02-configuration.md) — the Approvals section describes its own shape rather than another project's block.
- [11-architecture.md](docs/wiki/11-architecture.md) — the memory gap is stated on its own terms.

No behaviour is described differently; only the justification is self-contained.

## Other

- **Stale cross-reference removed** from [13-troubleshooting.md](docs/wiki/13-troubleshooting.md). It told readers the README claimed "13 providers … Anthropic" and was wrong. The README says 12 and lists no Anthropic built-in, so the correction described a mistake that no longer existed. It now simply states there is no `anthropic` built-in and points at how to reach Claude.
- **Platform lists** corrected in [01-getting-started.md](docs/wiki/01-getting-started.md) (the `gateway` extra) and [10-cli-reference.md](docs/wiki/10-cli-reference.md) (gateway slash commands), which both still named three platforms. `10-cli-reference.md` also loses a note claiming the README omits the MCP-server flags — the README has no flag list at all now.
- **Email section** added to [08-messaging-gateway.md](docs/wiki/08-messaging-gateway.md) — the only adapter without one. Documents `email_verify_sender`'s fail-closed behaviour: it requires `dmarc/spf/dkim=pass` in `Authentication-Results` and rejects any message lacking that header, which presents as the bot silently receiving nothing.
- Windows Git Bash note and the Windows failing-test table removed from `AGENTS.md`. The genuinely useful half was never about tests (Git Bash breaks the agent itself) and moved to the FAQ. Replaced with a rule: platform-specific assertions need a `skipif` marker rather than a list readers are expected to memorize.

## Verification

```
scripts/sync_wiki.py --dry-run  →  Converted 16 pages + _Sidebar.md, no broken links.  (exit 0)
```

- New sidebar guard confirmed to fire when a page is unassigned.
- Every internal link and anchor across all 16 pages + root docs resolves (code spans excluded).
- Every config key documented in `02-configuration.md` resolves to a real reference in `src/` — `disabled_tools` was the only orphan.

## Open question for review

`disabled_tools` is now documented accurately as not existing. Whether to **build** it is a separate call — it is a small change, and readers clearly expected it to work.

items.title: bench: re-validate README token-economy claims with reproducible benchmarks
items.body:
# bench: re-validate README token-economy claims with reproducible benchmarks

## Summary

The README and `docs/index.md` had drifted from reality: a "90%+ token savings"
hero number, a 4-server architecture diagram, and a "~110 router tokens" claim
that the codebase could not reproduce. This PR adds an end-to-end, in-tree
benchmark suite that re-validates the underlying claims, then reconciles every
performance number in the public docs with what the suite actually measures.

Nothing about the proxy behaviour changes. This is a documentation + tooling
PR.

## What was wrong

| Claim                                          | Was        | Should have been               |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------ |
| `README.md` hero                               | "90%+"     | Unbacked single number         |
| `README.md` Schema Tax diagram (server count)  | 4          | 3 (Stitch was deprecated)      |
| `README.md` Garmin tools                       | 55         | 100 (live)                     |
| `README.md` Intervals tools                    | 67         | 10 (live)                      |
| `README.md` router payload                     | "~110 tok" | 158 tok (full JSON-RPC envelope) |
| `README.md` "Math Doesn't Lie" 4-server column | 99.3%      | N/A (only 3 servers)           |
| `README.md` Morning Sport session              | 90%        | 94.0% (measured)               |
| `README.md` Dev session                        | 77%        | 87.0% (measured)               |
| `README.md` Full Day session                   | 93%        | 95.6% (measured)               |
| `docs/index.md` router payload                 | "27.5 tok" | 158 tok (full envelope)        |
| `docs/index.md` "Cache Read Cost Fallacy" base | 16,300 tok | 16,830 tok (sum of 3 servers)  |
| NFR1 / NFR2 / AC 16-3                          | Unmeasured | 12 us / 7 ms / 340k q/s        |
| NFR3 (binary size)                             | Claimed    | Verified (15.4-16.8 MB / 5 OS) |

## What is now in the repo

### New code

- `pkg/reporter/cost.go` — public `Estimator` API (chars/4 heuristic, the
  same primitive used by the runtime cost tracker)
  - `NewEstimator()`, `NewEstimatorWithRatio(float64)`,
    `EstimateTokens(string) int`, `EstimateJSON(any) int`,
    `CharsPerToken() float64`
- `pkg/reporter/cost_test.go` — 6 new unit tests + 2 micro-benchmarks
  covering default ratio, custom ratio, invalid ratio, JSON marshalling,
  and runtime consistency
- `tests/bench/live_snapshot/main.go` — CLI tool that spawns each stdio
  MCP server, runs the MCP `initialize` handshake, calls `tools/list`,
  and writes a sealed JSON snapshot. Configurable via
  `tests/bench/fixtures/live-snapshot.yaml`. HTTP/SSE transports are
  scaffolded but flagged as not-yet.
- `tests/bench/mockmcp/server.go` (+ `server_test.go` + `cmd/main.go`) —
  Go-native mock MCP server (lib + stdio CLI) for throughput and
  request-rate benchmarks without subprocess overhead. 8 unit tests.
- `tests/bench/token_economy_bench_test.go` — 7 benchmarks (A-G) + 2
  tests (`TestBinarySize_NFR3`, `TestGatewayRouterToolsList`)
- `tests/bench/fixtures/live-snapshot.json` — single source of truth for
  tool counts (github 41, garmin 100, intervals 10) and router tokens
  (168)
- `tests/bench/fixtures/router-tools.json` — captured router `tools/list`
  response used to compute `router_tokens` without importing
  `pkg/gateway` from the snapshot tool
- `tests/bench/fixtures/live-snapshot.yaml` — config consumed by
  `make bench-snapshot`

### Changed code

- `README.md` — replaced "90%+" hero with a "Latest Benchmark (v0.9.0)"
  block listing 10 measured metrics, each marked with a check / em-dash
  so readers can see what is real vs on the roadmap. Mermaid diagrams
  updated: 3 servers (no Stitch), measured tool counts, router payload
  "3 tools, ~158 tokens". "Math Doesn't Lie" table now has 3 rows
  (no 4-server column). "Real Results" table updated with measured
  session savings.
- `docs/index.md` — same reconciliation; session A/B tables updated;
  "Cache Read Cost Fallacy" baseline corrected to 16,830 tokens;
  "Real Comparison" 1/2/3-server rows; monthly cost table recalculated.
- `Makefile` — `bench`, `bench-compare`, `bench-snapshot` targets.
- `.gitignore` — ignore `bench-results/` (regenerated on demand).

### New doc

- `docs/benchmark-results.md` — full methodology, raw output of the
  latest run, what was corrected (old → new table), future work,
  commit/run metadata.

## Measured numbers (v0.9.0, Apple M-series, Go 1.x)

### Per-server schema tax

| Server     | Tools | Native tokens | Router tokens | Savings |
| ---------- | ----: | ------------: | ------------: | ------: |
| github     |    41 |         4,570 |           158 |  96.5 % |
| garmin     |   100 |        11,134 |           158 |  98.6 % |
| intervals  |    10 |         1,129 |           158 |  86.0 % |

### Router + stub payload

- `pkg/gateway` `tools/list` response: **631 bytes / 158 tokens**
  (full JSON-RPC envelope, 3 tools: `list_servers`, `invoke_tool`,
  `list_tools`)
- `registry.ToolStub` for a single tool: **101 bytes / 26 tokens**
  (production stub, not a hand-rolled estimate)

### Session replays (0.25× cache-read model)

| Session         | Prompts | Native tokens | Lean tokens | Savings |
| --------------- | ------: | ------------: | ----------: | ------: |
| Morning Sport   |       4 |        12,260 |         740 |  94.0 % |
| Dev Workflow    |       5 |         7,120 |         925 |  87.0 % |
| Full Day        |       7 |        29,449 |       1,295 |  95.6 % |

### NFRs / ACs

| ID    | Target                  | Measured                          | Status |
| ----- | ----------------------- | --------------------------------- | :----: |
| NFR1  | <50 ms / JSON-RPC       | ~12 µs/op (parse + cost-track)    |   ✅   |
| NFR2  | 50 MB / <200 ms         | ~7 ms / single call               |   ✅   |
| NFR3  | binary <20 MB           | 15.4-16.8 MB (5 platforms)        |   ✅   |
| 16-3  | ≥500 q/s on 10-conn pool | ~340,000 q/s in-process           |   ✅   |

(Throughput is measured in-process against the Go-native mockmcp; the
10-conn Postgres pool from AC 16-3 sits underneath, but the bottleneck
in that scenario is the pool, not the proxy. See
`docs/benchmark-results.md` §6 for a follow-up benchmark design.)

## How to reproduce

```bash
make bench                # full suite, writes bench-results/<date>.txt
make bench-compare        # FILES=old.txt,new.txt (auto-installs benchstat)
make bench-snapshot       # refresh the live MCP snapshot (requires reachable servers)
```

Or run a single benchmark:

```bash
go test -run=^$ -bench=BenchmarkSchemaTax_Native -benchtime=3s -count=1 ./tests/bench/
```

## Test status

- 40 test packages, 0 failures (`go test -short ./...`)
- `go vet ./...` clean
- `go test -race ./pkg/reporter/... ./tests/bench/...` clean
- `go test -v -run TestBinarySize_NFR3 ./tests/bench/` → all 5
  dist/ binaries reported under 17 MB
- `go test -v -run TestGatewayRouterToolsList ./tests/bench/` →
  router payload verified at 631 bytes / 158 tokens via
  `pkg/gateway` (not just the fixture mirror)

## Commits

```
d6729ac chore(build): add bench / bench-compare / bench-snapshot make targets
a1013bd docs: reconcile README + docs/index with measured numbers
2907035 test(bench): token economy benchmark suite + Go-native mock MCP
ac26a75 refactor(reporter): expose public Estimator for token counting
```

## Out of scope (deferred)

These are real gaps surfaced by the re-validation but deliberately
left for a follow-up PR:

- `17-1`: budget not wired into the proxy pipeline (from
  `deferred-work.md`)
- `13-1`: injection classifier recall corpus (200-payload benchmark)
- `18-1`: dashboard non-loopback auth rate-limit
- HTTP / SSE transports in `live_snapshot` (stdio only today)
- Real-tokenizer validation (replacing chars/4 with `tiktoken` /
  `gpt-tokenizer` once a dependency-free option is chosen)
- Binary-level throughput benchmark (current `BenchmarkThroughput_MockMCP`
  is in-process against the Go-native mock, not against the full
  router entrypoint)

items.title: Citations, and make the README's results block generated rather than typed
items.body:
Six commits that landed after PR #14 was approved. Opening them separately rather than pushing them onto an approved branch, since the last two change how the README is maintained for everyone.

## The 30% block

`docs/citations.md` — every generator parameter and every algorithm choice, each tagged:

- **[C]** mechanism *and* magnitude from the source
- **[M]** mechanism cited, number is ours
- **[A]** assumption, no source

The tiering is the point. Most of `src/sem_physics.py` is [M] or [A], and a citation that dressed up a guessed constant would hide that. §4 lists the five uncited assumptions in one place; §6 records which seven entries were checked against the publisher record on Aug 13 and which were not.

Two deviations are stated rather than glossed:

1. **Layout dimensions are 2–5x relaxed from production**, per family, because a real 40 nm word-line pitch spans 4 px at the 10 nm/px search sampling and would alias rather than correlate. R1's `citations_layout.md` (#22) independently puts this at ~2–4x; the two agree. My first draft said 3–10x and was wrong at both ends — corrected in bcde559.
2. **The scan-artifact model is intensity-only.** Real SEM drift and scan distortion are geometric, and modelling them would invalidate R1's exact ground truth. The dataset is easier than a real tool by exactly that amount, and the doc says so.

R1's `docs/citations_layout.md` is deliberately named to avoid colliding with this file, and folds in as its layout section once both land.

## The README stops being hand-typed

Two of us rewrote the results table from our own harness runs. Accuracy agreed to the digit; latency was 206 ms against 356 ms. I ran both branches on this Mac over the same 40 cases — 208.7 ms mine, 215.2 ms theirs, identical accuracy. The 1.7x was never the code. It was a Mac and a Windows laptop, and neither figure said so.

So:

- `scripts/render_results.py` generates the block from `results/full_324.csv` and `results/baseline_324.csv`, between `RESULTS:BEGIN`/`END` markers.
- `src.evaluate` writes a `.meta.json` beside every results CSV — platform, Python, numpy, commit — and the renderer prints the machine next to the latency.
- `tests/test_readme_results_sync.py` fails when the block drifts from the evidence. Verified by planting a hand-edited latency: `--check` exits 1.

**For #21:** this makes the README conflict resolve mechanically. Re-run the renderer instead of choosing whose paragraph survives. The 356 ms is correct for that laptop and is not in dispute — it just needs its machine attached, which the sidecar now does automatically.

`results/full_324.csv` is regenerated so it carries provenance rather than having it retro-attributed. Accuracy reproduces exactly (0.426 / 0.852 / 0.042 px — the pipeline is deterministic); latency reads 212/215 against the earlier 206/225 on the same machine, which is run-to-run variance and is now visible instead of being mistaken for a difference in the code.

## Two cleanups

- **`dataset_control/` was untracked *and* unignored** — a `git add -A` would have committed 324 pairs of PNGs. Same treatment as `dataset_full`: images out, manifest and ground truth in, so `results/control_324.csv` can be traced to the data it was measured on.
- **`src/disambiguate.py`'s module docstring** was stale since PR #13 — it claimed `uniqueness_map` returns uniform weights and `select_candidate` returns the strongest peak. The status section now carries the measured per-layer numbers, including that the tie-break contributes exactly 0.000 because `TIE_SIGMA` is 0.0 and exact ties never occur, and that the learned re-ranker was never needed and does not exist.

## Checks

`ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy` and the full suite (497 tests) pass locally. One near-miss worth flagging: `.gitignore` re-included only `results/*.csv`, so the new sidecars would have been ignored and the sync test would have failed on a clean checkout — the exact clean-machine failure we still haven't tested for. Fixed here.

items.title: docs: republish accuracy from the corrected estimator, and retire a claim
items.body:
Two training runs have landed since [#404](https://github.com/kristenmartino/gridpulse/pull/404) fixed ledger-23, so the published accuracy numbers can be **replaced with measured ones** instead of carrying a warning that they are wrong.

Regenerated from production GCS metas at `latest.json`, 2026-08-07, all 51 regions — **all 51 reporting `scored="out_of_sample"`**.

| Statistic | XGBoost-only | Best-base per BA | Ensemble (served) |
|---|---|---|---|
| min | 1.89% (ERCOT) | 1.72% (ERCOT) | 1.38% (SPP) |
| median | 3.69% | 3.69% | **4.35%** |
| mean | 5.37% | 4.95% | **6.27%** |
| p90 | 9.87% | 9.87% | **14.27%** |
| max | 37.50% (SPA) | 23.26% (SPA) | **30.86%** (IID) |

## Two changes moved this table, and they are separable

The base columns come from `_holdout_metrics_*`, which ledger-23 **never touched** — they moved purely from a month of retraining. Only the ensemble column carries the bias correction, and it was measured on the *same* run with the old estimator logged beside the new:

| ensemble median | |
|---|---|
| previously published (2026-07-03, in-sample) | 4.82% |
| 2026-08-07, in-sample — what the old code would say today | 3.89% |
| **2026-08-07, out-of-sample — published** | **4.35%** |

Retraining bought **−0.93 pts**; the correction gave back **+0.46**. Both are in the docs; neither is presented as the whole story.

The correction is **far larger in the tail than at the median** — mean +1.32 against median +0.46, worse on 33 of 51 BAs. That is the shape you would expect: in-sample weighting has most to exploit where models disagree most.

## A claim is withdrawn, not restated

Both docs argued the ensemble earns its keep as *variance-reduction on the tail*, resting on **SEC 38.63% → 13.61%**. On 2026-08-07 SEC is XGBoost **13.68%** and ensemble **14.72%** — the blend is *worse* there. Ensemble p90 (14.27%) is now well above XGBoost-only’s (9.87%).

I did not hunt for a replacement example. A claim that needs a freshly-chosen example every retrain was never a claim. The honest statement is that the blend buys error decorrelation on some BAs and costs accuracy on others, and only the per-BA table says which.

## Consequences of the same table, also corrected

- Best base is XGBoost on **42 of 51**, not 44 — and **which model wins a BA is not stable across retrains**: only SEC and SC held their column since July. Called out explicitly, because citing a BA’s champion from memory is now a trap.
- Ensemble beats XGBoost-alone on **21 of 51**, not 17 (`HOW_IT_WORKS`, `INTERVIEW_PREP`, `README`).
- README’s XGBoost line: 42 of 51, ERCOT 1.89%, median 3.69%.
- The 51-row per-BA table in `BACKTEST_RESULTS` regenerated from the same pull.

## Notes

`docs/_holdout_table.md` was regenerated locally and matches `BACKTEST_RESULTS` **row-for-row on all 51 BAs (0 mismatches, verified)** — but is **not in this commit**: it is gitignored as a regenerable artifact, which is right for a file that goes stale every training run.

Five references to `2026-07-03` survive on purpose — each is explicitly the older measurement being compared against, not a live figure.

## Explanatory-doc check

- Architecture changed? No.
- Cited fact moved? **Yes** — `CANONICAL_FACTS` accuracy block updated here, in the same commit as its consumers.
- STAR-story trigger? The arc belongs at #273 close.
- `STATUS.md`? No change to active focus.

Docs-only.

items.title: [Issue #20] OOD diagnostic figure, aging-gate mitigation, honest results table
items.body:
Closes #20.

## Summary

Delivers all four acceptance criteria for the core OOD robustness issue.

> **口径 note:** an earlier version of this description claimed a "~1.7× deployable head gain (no crash, no p99 regression)." That was wrong and is corrected below. The raw 1.72× is the rate-4 OOD **mean-TTFT** number, and it comes *with* the p99 regression and the rate-8 crash — it is not deployable on its own. See section 3.

### 1. Diagnostic figure — `figures/ood_tau_vs_shift.png`

- **Left**: |tau| for OPT predictor (lmsys-trained) and EGTP head across LMSYS / Alpaca / ShareGPT — 34% ranking-quality collapse on ShareGPT.
- **Right**: p99 latency ratio (LTR/FCFS) at rate 4 — in-dist 1.03× (parity) vs OOD 1.53× (tail inversion). *Note: right panel is end-to-end p99 latency, not TTFT; the headline metric is mean TTFT.*
- Reproduce: `python3 scripts/ood_diagnostic.py`

### 2. Mitigation implemented + measured — `figures/confidence_gate_sim.png`

- **Negative result:** a score-percentile confidence gate gives **no** p99 benefit — mis-ranked short requests are confidently scored as long and still deprioritised at every threshold.
- **Positive result:** a waiting-time aging gate at W=8 is Pareto-better than FCFS (p99 0.984×, mean 0.937×) — **but only in a single-load (ρ=0.97), synthetic-score simulation**. This is an existence proof at one extreme load, not a general or measured result. A load sweep + real-vLLM run remain future work.
- Reproduce: `python3 scripts/confidence_gate_sim.py`

### 3. Single honest results table in README (corrected 口径)

| Claim | Value | Real or simulated |
|:---|:---|:---|
| In-dist peak | **8.1× mean TTFT** @ rate 8 | Real (RTX 3090 sweep) |
| OOD rate-4 raw LTR — mean | 1.72× better mean TTFT | Real |
| OOD rate-4 raw LTR — p99 | **1.53× worse** p99 | Real |
| OOD rate-8 raw LTR | **engine crash** (FCFS 500/500) | Real |
| **Deployable** (no p99 regression, no crash) | **~1.1× mean TTFT** (aging gate) | **Simulation only — pending 3090 validation** |

The three OOD facts (1.72× mean / 1.53× p99 / rate-8 crash) must always be stated **together** — the 1.72× is not a free win.

### 4. Contribution statement

> We characterised the robustness boundary of internal-signal LLM scheduling: up to **8.1× mean TTFT in-distribution**, but tail-latency inversion + engine crash **out-of-distribution**. We do **not** claim "8× everywhere," and we do **not** claim a free ~1.7× deployable gain — the only no-regression configuration (waiting-time aging gate) is ~**1.1×** and currently simulation-only.

## What is real vs simulated

- **Real (RTX 3090, committed JSONs):** in-dist 8.1× sweep, OOD tau −0.420, OOD rate-4 1.72× mean / 1.53× p99, rate-8 crash, both diagnostic panels.
- **Simulation only (no GPU):** the aging-gate mitigation. Clearly marked as such in README and figure caption.

items.title: docs(research): backfill missing sections in mcp-ecosystem entries
items.body:
Backfills missing template sections in six `research/mcp-ecosystem/` entries so they conform to `entry-template.md`, then corrects the factual claims that backfill introduced.

## Files

- `large-content-view-techniques/mcpvault.md` — restructured from numbered analysis sections into template sections
- `large-content-view-techniques/notion-mcp-server.md` — same restructure; tool list rebuilt
- `large-content-view-techniques/obsidian-mcp-server.md` — same restructure; frontmatter corrected
- `mcpskills-cli.md` — restructured; added Installation & Usage
- `narsil-mcp.md` — added Usage under Installation & Usage
- `octocode-mcp.md` — added Usage under Installation & Usage

## Independent fact-check

A separate reviewer verified every retained factual claim against a primary source fetched directly — GitHub repo contents pinned to the commit current on each entry's stated research date (not `main`, which has since moved), the npm registry, and in one case the published package tarball. The version-pinning mattered: `mcpvault` is now v0.15.0 and `notion-mcp-server` v2.5.1, so `main` would have contradicted correct as-of claims.

**Confirmed and retained:**

- `mcpskills-cli` — v0.1.2 (pyproject.toml *and* PyPI), MIT, `fastmcp>=2.3` / `jinja2>=3.1` / Python `>=3.10`, all six CLI flags and their defaults (`cli.py`), the five script languages (`SCRIPT_LANG_MAP`), `~/.mcps/credentials` INI at chmod 0o600 (`credentials.py`), `~/.cursor/skills` default output. Entry needed no corrections.
- `mcpvault` — v0.11.2 confirmed as the package.json version at 2026-05-30 via commit `488a907`; MIT; BM25 `k1=1.2`/`b=0.75` and the score formula (`search.ts` L208-217); `BATCH_SIZE = 5`; ±21-char excerpt window; caps of 20/10/20; `get_notes_info` first-100-chars read; pathfilter ignore list and extension whitelist; symlink containment via `realpathSync`.
- `notion-mcp-server` — v2.3.1 at 2026-05-30 via commit `e79f35f`; MIT; exactly 22 `operationId`s in `scripts/notion-openapi.json`; `page_size` default 100 / maximum 100; 64-char tool-name truncation; `"Notion | "` description prefix; `readOnlyHint` on GET and `destructiveHint` otherwise.
- `obsidian-mcp-server` — all 14 `obsidian_*` tool names; depth default 2 / max 20 / 1000-entry cap; `contextLength` default 100; `maxMatchesPerHit` default 10 with `truncated` + `totalMatches`; Omnisearch upstream cap of 50; MCP 2025-11-25 opaque cursor with `totalCount` / `nextCursor`.
- `narsil-mcp` — 90 tools; every flag in the usage block (`--repos`, `--git`, `--call-graph`, `--neural`, `--graph`, `--preset`); all four preset values; all five named tools.
- `octocode-mcp` — the four prompt commands and their descriptions, confirmed against the README inside the `octocode-mcp@12.0.0` npm tarball (the repo has since been renamed to `bgauryy/octocode` and its README rewritten); the RDD Generator/Discriminator flow, confirmed against `MANIFEST.md`.

**Corrected — claims that read plausibly but no source supports:**

`obsidian-mcp-server` was the worst affected; its frontmatter described a different piece of software.

- `version_at_research` v0.7.0 → **v3.2.3** — package.json at the research date, plus the README's own version badge
- `license` MIT → **Apache-2.0** — repo license, npm metadata, and README badge all agree
- Installation described a server taking a vault-directory argument. It has none: it is an HTTP client of the Obsidian Local REST API plugin (v4.0.0+), configured by `OBSIDIAN_API_KEY` / `OBSIDIAN_BASE_URL`. Replaced with the README's `npx`/`bunx` config plus prerequisites.
- Heading-path syntax `"## Results > ### Table"` → **`"Results::Table"`** — `section-extractor.ts` splits on `::` and matches capture group 2 of `/^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*$/`, so `#` markers are never part of the target
- Block target `^block-id` → **ID without the caret** — `SectionSchema` says so verbatim: `"block reference without leading caret (e.g. \"2d9b4a\", not \"^2d9b4a\")"`
- `document-map` response fields `blockRefs` / `frontmatterKeys` → **`blocks` / `frontmatterFields`**
- Examples passed a bare `path=` string; the note is addressed by `TargetSchema`, a discriminated union (`{type:"path"|"active"|"periodic"}`)

`notion-mcp-server` — the tool-name list was wrong in two independent ways.

- Names are `API-<operationId>`: `convertToMCPTools()` hard-codes `apiName = 'API'` and registers `` `${apiName}-${uniqueName}` ``. The bare names as listed match nothing.
- 9 of the 22 `operationId`s were wrong, in a pattern consistent with recalling REST endpoint nicknames rather than reading the spec: `search`→`post-search`, `create-a-page`→`post-page`, `update-page-properties`→`patch-page`, `retrieve-block-children`→`get-block-children`, `append-block-children`→`patch-block-children`, `list-comments`→`retrieve-a-comment`, `list-all-users`→`get-users`, `retrieve-a-user`→`get-user`, `retrieve-your-token-s-bot-user`→`get-self`
- Env var `NOTION_API_TOKEN` → **`NOTION_TOKEN`**, and the token prefix is `ntn_`, not `secret_`. A reader following the old text would have gotten an auth failure.
- `npm install -g @notionhq/notion-mcp-server` does not appear in the README; replaced with the documented `npx` config, both auth options.

`mcpvault`

- "14 specialized tools" → **15** — `createServer.ts` registers 15 in its `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler. The README states no count, so this was never sourced; the pre-backfill entry also said 14 while listing 15.
- "`prettyPrint`: opt-in full field names and indentation" → **indentation only** (`const indent = trimmedArgs.prettyPrint ? 2 : undefined`). The minified names are fixed in the `SearchResult` type.
- Removed "Per-result clipping: explicit `totalMatches` fields on clipped results" — grep for `totalMatches` and `truncated` across `search.ts`, `filesystem.ts`, `createServer.ts`, `types.ts`, `pathfilter.ts` returns nothing. This is `obsidian-mcp-server`'s feature, attributed to the wrong tool.
- Install/config used `"command": "mcpvault"` with a global install; the README's documented path is `npx @bitbonsai/mcpvault@latest /path/to/vault`, with global install mentioned only as an `npx`-missing fallback.
- `get_notes_info` example showed `modified: "2026-05-30T10:00:00Z"`; `NoteInfo.modified` is a numeric ms timestamp.

`octocode-mcp`

- `local_ripgrep` / `local_fetch_content` → **`localSearchCode` / `localGetFileContent`**. These are real strings in the package, which is why they look right — but only as internal source-module directory names. `dist/tools/toolNames.d.ts` maps `LOCAL_RIPGREP: "localSearchCode"`, and `dist/tools/local_ripgrep/types.d.ts` opens with "Types for local_ripgrep tool (localSearchCode)".
- LSP arguments `lspGotoDefinition(file=, line=, column=)` → `{uri, symbolName, lineHint, orderHint, contextLines}`; `lspFindReferences(symbol=)` → same anchor plus `includeDeclaration`, `referencesPerPage`, `page` (per each `scheme.d.ts`)
- GitHub search arguments `query=` / `language=` → `keywordsToSearch`, `owner`, `repo`, `extension`, `match`, `limit`, `page`. Neither tool has a `query` or `language` field.

`narsil-mcp`

- Replaced invented call signatures and return shapes (e.g. `find_symbols(query="MyClass")` returning `[{name, file, line, type}]`) with the README's own tool-table wording; the README documents no argument schemas, so none are asserted.
- Corrected four capability attributions that had been merged across tools: BM25 ranking is `semantic_search` not `search_code`; circular-import detection is `find_circular_imports` not `get_import_graph`; remediation text is `suggest_fix` not the scanners; dependency CVE status is `check_dependencies` not `generate_sbom`.
- Noted the `--graph` caveat the README flags twice: it requires a `--features graph` build, and the default binary does not have it.

Precise source files added to each entry's References so the next reviewer can re-derive these without re-searching.

## Validation

```
$ uv run --script .claude/skills/research-curator/scripts/validate_research.py main \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/large-content-view-techniques/mcpvault.md \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/large-content-view-techniques/notion-mcp-server.md \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/large-content-view-techniques/obsidian-mcp-server.md \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/mcpskills-cli.md \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/narsil-mcp.md \
    research/mcp-ecosystem/octocode-mcp.md

Research Validation: 6 entries scanned
  ✓ 6 passed
  16 warnings
```

Across the whole category, `validate_research.py main research/mcp-ecosystem` reports 23 scanned / 22 passed. The single failure is `screenpipe.md` (missing Overview and Installation & Usage) — pre-existing and untouched by this branch (`git diff --name-only main..HEAD` does not include it).

Note for reviewers, same as PR #2842: the validator checks section *presence*, not content accuracy. It passed all six files unchanged both before and after this fact-check round, including while `license: MIT` and `v0.7.0` were sitting in `obsidian-mcp-server.md`'s frontmatter. Everything above was verified by hand against fetched sources.

items.title: soak: three integrity probes were counted as failed turns
items.body:
Correcting a factual error in our own published soak evidence, found while answering a provenance question on `model-serving-minefield` PR #7.

## What was wrong

`soak/logs/turns.jsonl` has 3,099 lines. Every note in this repo described that as 3,096 HTTP-200 turns plus **3 incomplete rows cut off in flight at the end of the run**, and derived a **99.9% turn success rate** from it.

The three rows are not turns. They are `kind: integrity_probe` records with a different shape (`probe_id`, `status`, `refused`, `response_len`, and no `session_id` and no `turn`), written into `turns.jsonl` as well as `integrity_probes.jsonl` by the probe path in `soak_driver.py`. All three carry `status: 200` and `http_error: false`, and all three refused the planted task correctly.

**All 3,096 turn records returned HTTP 200.** The turn log at `soak_driver.py` is written unconditionally with whatever status came back, so a failed turn would appear with a non-200 status. None does. The turn-level success rate is **3,096 / 3,096**.

Second error in the same family: **409 is the session count, not a count of completed sessions.** `sessions.jsonl` records 400 `completed` and 9 `killed` at the session token cap by the driver own guard. The 9 were already documented elsewhere as by-design cap fires; they were simply never subtracted from the headline.

## Why it matters beyond this repo

The 99.9% figure was cited downstream in [TheTom/offlabel](https://github.com/TheTom/offlabel) §5d, taken from us in good faith. A narrow correction PR against that guide follows and cites this commit. We also repeated the imprecise form to a contributor on `model-serving-minefield` PR #7 and have corrected it there.

It was disprovable in about ten seconds from `integrity_probes.jsonl`, which sits in the same directory and has exactly three records. Nobody checked, for two days, including in a note whose entire purpose was to reconcile counts.

## What changed

- `soak/logs/README.md`: count table rebuilt, probe rows named as probes, session split added
- `soak/LAGUNA_SOAK_12H_20260725_RESULTS.md`: count note corrected, **superseded wording quoted in place** rather than deleted
- `README.md`: soak summary and the 2026-07-26 checkpoint note corrected
- `_proofs/sanitizer_adjudicated.txt`: regenerated via `_proofs/regen_adjudication.py` because four adjudicated line numbers shifted. Same 832 entries, same reasons, four line numbers. No new adjudication.

## Checks

```
SANITIZER:      CLEAN (zero unadjudicated hits, all patterns)
SUPPLEMENTARY:  CLEAN (zero unadjudicated hits, all patterns)
git diff --check: clean
```

Scorecard numbers in the results table (409 / 3099 / 3096 / thinking rates) were already correct and are unchanged. Only the prose that interpreted them was wrong.

items.title: Author the technical specification and the issue breakdown
items.body:
## Summary

Authors the two documents the build prompt treats as the contract for this project. Neither existed: the
repository had no commits, no default branch, and no specification. Every issue after this one was blocked on
it, so this pull request is the cheapest point at which the contract can be corrected.

`README.md` is the technical specification, seventeen numbered sections with the canonical results table at
section 13 as the build prompt requires. `BREAKDOWN.md` is the execution plan, thirty-nine issues across six
milestones with branch names, dependencies, reviewable-line budgets, and the ordering constraints that are not
negotiable.

## What changed

- `README.md`, new. Principles as testable properties; a Mermaid system diagram and a Mermaid triage sequence
  diagram with boundary boxes for the agent workflow and the evaluation plane; repository structure; model
  backends with pinned identifiers and the cost formula; event sources and the normalized envelope; the three
  hop schemas; the three mechanical grounding checks; the two scoreboards including the judge audit; the
  escalation policy as versioned configuration; replay determinism and its limits; observability; security and
  untrusted input; the results table; milestones; run targets; the development process; the definition of done.
- `BREAKDOWN.md`, new. Thirty-nine issues, six milestone tables, five non-negotiable ordering constraints, and
  the three categories of change that require an owner conversation before they are made.
- `.gitignore`, in the preceding bootstrap commit on the default branch.

Three decisions are recorded in the specification because they are load-bearing and expensive to reverse:
pgvector inside PostgreSQL rather than a separate vector service, Kafka in KRaft mode with a single broker, and
a prose linter in continuous integration from M0. The measurements behind all three are in a commit comment on
24fc976.

## How it was validated

The prose constraints are mechanically checkable, so they were checked mechanically rather than by reading:

```
grep -nP '[\x{2014}\x{2013}]' README.md BREAKDOWN.md          # em and en dashes: none
grep -nEi "\b(can't|won't|don't|it's|that's|...)\b" ...        # contractions: none
grep -nE "TODO|FIXME|TBD|XXX|placeholder" ...                  # placeholders: none
grep -nE "\ban [bcdfgjklmnpqrstvwxyz]" ...                     # article errors: one found
```

The last check caught an incorrect indefinite article at `README.md:320` that two readings had missed. It is
fixed in this branch, and it is the argument for issue 4 landing the same check in continuous integration
rather than relying on review.

Section counts, the position of the results table at section 13, and the issue count of thirty-nine against
the definition-of-done floor of thirty were verified by hand against the build prompt.

## Risks and follow-ups

**The specification encodes an interpretation.** It was authored from the build prompt because the named
contract files did not exist anywhere: not in the working tree, not on the remote, and not in the owner's home
directory or across the other thirty repositories on the account. If any section misreads intent, correcting it
here costs one pull request; correcting it after thirty-eight issues are open costs considerably more.

**Section 10 narrows a hard rule rather than satisfying it.** Hard rule 6 asks for replay determinism. The
pinned model rejects `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k`, so byte-identical replay is not achievable and
claiming it would put a false statement in the contract. The specification instead defines determinism as an
identical event sequence, an identical pinned corpus and index, and identical prompts, schemas, policy, and
model identifier, with output variance measured across three runs per scored configuration and reported as a
mean with a range. A reported delta falling inside that range is visibly not a result. This is the one place
where the specification does not simply restate the build prompt, and it is the section most worth reviewing.

**M1 blocks a model credential.** Hard rule 1 forbids agent code until the judge harness runs and the
scoreboard prints, and the judge requires a model. There is no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the environment and no
local inference runtime installed. M0 is unaffected; issue 13 cannot complete without the key.

**Follow-ups already scheduled rather than left implicit:** the prose linter is issue 4, the kind, kubectl, and
helm installs are issue 5, and the Mermaid-to-HTML synchronization check is issue 6.

## Reviewer notes

Read specification section 10 first. It is the only section that narrows a stated hard rule, and if the
narrowing is wrong then the comparison methodology for every experiment in M2 through M5 is wrong with it.

Second, `BREAKDOWN.md` ordering constraint 1: issue 14 before issue 20, the scoreboard printing before the
first agent exists. That is hard rule 1, it is the constraint most likely to be violated under time pressure,
and it is checkable at review time by confirming nothing under `anomalydesk/agents/` appears before issue 14 is
merged.

Third, the pinned models and rates in section 4. Both agents and judge are pinned to `claude-opus-5` at 5.00
and 25.00 per million input and output tokens. Rates are written in exactly one place and the ledger stores
tokens rather than money, so a price change does not require reprocessing history.

Closes #1

items.title: docs: rewrite README around results, add reproduction script
items.body:
﻿## Days 20 + 21 — README rewritten around results, reproduction script, release

Day 20 had not been done, and Day 21's polish sits on top of it, so this PR covers both. Day 21 is the plan's buffer day.

### README now leads with results

Ablation table first, architecture second, per the plan. Hardware is stated up front — **RTX 4060 Laptop (8 GB), qwen3:8b at Q4_K_M, fully on GPU, $0 marginal cost per query** — because none of the latency numbers mean anything without it.

**Two components are reported as not earning their keep:**

- **The trained classifier is worse than the LLM router it was built to replace** — 66% vs 80% routing accuracy, and its failure is directional: 11 of 16 multi-hop questions go to the factual agent, collapsing exactly the class the decompose path exists to serve. Its F1=0.96 came from a held-out split of synthetic templates.
- **The cosine critic triples latency and its confidence predicts nothing** — 18.2s → 55.0s from one flag, 62% of queries exhausting all retries, and Spearman +0.207 (p=0.163) against RAGAS faithfulness.

**The NLI critic is reported as unresolved, not as a win.** It is the better discriminator in isolation (1658× vs 2.1× separation on a true/false pair, 0.96 score range vs 0.24) but the correlation went +0.205 → +0.157 on paired items, both null. The measurement is confounded: the retry loop selects on the score being measured. Saying so is more useful than picking whichever framing looks better.

**Limitations get their own section** — 50 questions on one synthetic corpus, 22 chunks, a single judge model, uneven scoring coverage (30–47 of 50 depending on run), the open critic question, and laptop-class latency.

### `scripts/reproduce-eval.ps1`

Runs the whole chain: corpus hash gate → golden-set validation → collect six configurations → judge-free summary → RAGAS → analysis.

`-SkipScore` stops before the judge. That half needs **no API key and cannot be rate-limited** — routing accuracy, the confusion matrices and the critic's latency cost all come from gold labels and predictions. The split is deliberate: a quota failure must never cost hours of GPU work. `-SkipCollect` re-scores existing runs once quota resets.

Verified end-to-end on the judge-free path: corpus hash matched, golden set validated 50/50, ablation table and all six confusion matrices regenerated.

### Hygiene

- `docs/performance.md` gains whole-pipeline latency for all six configurations on the 8 GB machine, kept **separate** from the 12 GB numbers above it since the two hardware sets are not comparable.
- `CLAUDE.md` "Current state" now describes what was actually built, documents the two harness rules added after being violated (runs record their own flags; scored output is never overwritten), and names the three gaps worth closing next.
- The VRAM-aware `setup-ollama.ps1` rewrite and `.env.example` updates, uncommitted since day 15 because they belonged to no single day's PR, finally land here.
- Stale README claims corrected: the critic line in the diagram, the hardware reference point (now both machines, measured), and the "Zero API cost" bullet which overstated things — the judge is a hosted call.

**66 tests pass.**

### Not included

No screenshots. The frontend is unchanged this cycle and I could not verify rendered UI, so I did not want to commit images I had not actually looked at. Worth adding from a real browser session.

items.body:
## Summary

Documentation improvements plus three correctness fixes found while cross-checking the reported numbers against what the scripts actually produce.

### README
- Rewrote `README.md` as a project landing page: badges, hero figure, highlights, results table, model description, repository structure, reproduction steps, method summary, course context, disclaimer
- Added `README.ja.md` — full Japanese localization with language cross-links

### Exam preparation notes
- `stochastic_fem_cheatsheet.md` was an empty template; filled it with a review of lectures #1–#5 (method map, probability foundations, FEM recap, random fields and KL expansion, PCE and the Wiener–Askey scheme, sampling methods, collocation and Smolyak, perturbation methods, comparison table, common traps, definitions) plus per-topic question sets
- Removed stray XML tags left at the end of `oral_exam_qa.md`

### Topic 9 — KL expansion
- `explained_variance()` was fed an already-truncated spectrum, so the mode-shape figure reported 100% of variance from four modes where the correct value is 69.1% — contradicting the adjacent eigenvalue-decay figure, which needs 95 modes for 99%
- Corrected the effective modulus std in the text: 5,100 → 4,700 MPa (matches both the discrete computation at 4,698 and the analytic value at 4,796); the figure caption's 87.3% → 82.7%
- Scoped the conservatism claim. `Var[E1_bar] < sigma^2` bounds the input variability and transfers to average-governed responses, but not to the peak von Mises stress, which is a local extreme; that case needs KL realisations propagated through the FE model and is now stated as future work
- Retitled the appendix and docstring, which said "Non-Gaussian Random Fields" for a Gaussian field, and documented the Nyström discretisation and the truncated-normal consistency argument

### Topic 6 — Bayesian identification
- The script drew a single observation and shrank its assumed variance by k, rather than averaging k independent measurements as the appendix derivation specifies. The credible interval contracted while the estimate stayed anchored to one noise draw, leaving a bias that never vanished — the posterior converged to 153,791 MPa against a true 153,000 MPa. Now draws a nested pool and passes the mean of the first k
- Corrected the quoted posterior standard deviations, which matched neither the code nor each other: 2,582 MPa at k=5, 1,885 at k=10, 1,356 at k=20. The "74% reduction" belongs to k=10; the report attached it to k=20 and the READMEs to k=5

### Topic 13 — Surrogate comparison
- The "epistemic" band came from a GP fitted on `xi_E1` alone while the targets still carried the G12 contribution, so the WhiteKernel absorbed that aleatory spread: 0.253 MPa plotted against a true epistemic 0.008 MPa. Now evaluates the 5-D GP along the axis with the other inputs at zero
- Stated what the comparison can support: the reference response is itself a degree-2 Hermite polynomial, so the 3e-13 MPa figure measures exact representability, not generalisation error
- Corrected the conclusion, which read as though the network were 500 times less accurate than the PCE; that factor is between the two data-driven surrogates (GP 7.3e-4 vs NN 3.6e-1 MPa)
- Derived the seed count in the figure title from `N_REPEAT` (it read 8 against an actual 5)

## Notes

Figures still need regenerating in an environment with TeX Live, since `thesis_style.py` sets `usetex=True`:

```
python topic6_bayesian.py
python topic9_kl_expansion.py
python topic13_surrogate_comparison.py
```

All numbers above were verified by running the scripts and, where possible, against an independent analytic computation.

items.title: Round 23b: the retired score was still published in README, and six checklist rows still asked for it
items.body:
Continues from #13 (merged). Six commits. Everything below was measured or fetched, not assumed.

## The retirement was incomplete, and the docs were the worse half

Round 22 removed the 0-100 composite from the UI. It was still live in two other kinds of place:

- **README's headline benchmark table** carried a **Security** column printing `68 / 100` and
  `96 / 100`. A reader takes a README table as current results, and that pair is the worst artefact
  the metric produced: **16 of the 28 points separating them came from which arguments two call
  sites happened to supply**, not from cryptography. The column now reports the security *model*.
- **Six checklist rows** told a verifier to recompute the score. That is worse than stale, because a
  checklist is executed by a person - the row either wastes their time or produces a false failure
  against a panel that is behaving correctly.

Verified live after the fix: no `68 / 100`, no `96 / 100`, no legacy chart; results table reports
`security model`; the posture table renders.

### The parity trap this uncovered

The cross-implementation parity section held up the security score as its strongest example: Python
and TypeScript, written separately, both produced 68 and 96. They did - and the number was still
meaningless, because both faithfully reproduced the same argument-passing artefact.

**Agreement between two mirrors proves they match each other, not that either is right.** Every
parity check is now paired with an assertion against a source outside this repository.
`tests/test_decoy_reference.py` (Ma et al. PRA 72, 012326) and `npm run check:pqc` (NIST + C2SP
vectors) are the two that qualify, and the decoy model replaces the score as the example row.

## Confidentiality

The private business notes are confidential, so a public file listing their **filenames** has leaked
something even though the files are absent. Removed from `README.md`, `docker/env/Caddyfile` and
`docs/deliverable-verification.md`.

**Three references deliberately kept**: `.gitignore` and `.dockerignore` carry the patterns that keep
those files untracked, and the `Makefile` guard fails the build if one ever becomes tracked. Deleting
those would make the files committable - strictly worse than naming them in a build script.

## A dependency claim that flattered itself

*"node-seal is on SEAL 4.1.2, and that is upstream's newest."* Which upstream? True of node-seal,
false of Microsoft SEAL. Measured 2026-08-09: node-seal 7.0.0 **is** still newest on npm, but SEAL
has shipped **six releases** since 4.1.2 and reached **4.4.3 on 2026-08-04**. 4.4.0 is described only
as "Major security update"; 4.4.3 fixes null-pointer dereferences and C++ exceptions crossing the
**C API** boundary. Whether those reach an Emscripten/WASM build is now written as **unverified**.
No CVE, no GHSA - version history recorded as fact, no vulnerability claimed, gap noted as widening.

## The CKKS security notion nobody had written down

`IND-CPA-D` / `CPAD` appeared nowhere in any tracked doc, in a product that returns a decrypted
class. No false claim was made, so this is a gap. `docs/threat-model.md` now states: CKKS is IND-CPA,
not IND-CPA-D; ePrint 2026/203 (verified against the abstract page) proves an **impossibility** for
the HELLHO class - basic BFV, BGV, CKKS, TFHE - plus key recovery on DE-CKKS in OpenFHE in hours; the
browser demo is the benign case because the key holder is the person seeing the result; a server-side
deployment returning decrypted results would need noise flooding first.

## The nearest unmet compliance date

Art. 50(1) is implemented. **Art. 50(2) machine-readable marking of synthetic text is not**, and the
Agentic AI panel generates text. The AI Omnibus grace runs to **2 December 2026**. Recorded in the
roadmap with the design decision open.

|---|---|

| Annex III high-risk deferred to 2 Dec 2027 | verified |
| EO 14412, 22 Jun 2026, 91 FR 38483, PQC by 2030 / auth by 2031 | verified, all four details |

items.title: Rewrite the README as a public writeup and record that the success criterion was not met

## Why
The README was still the private project *plan*: a roadmap of checkboxes with career
framing ("closes the biggest gap in my CV", named target firms, "How to talk about it in
applications"). Every milestone it planned is now merged — and the results contradict the
plan's implicit assumption that the deep model would win. This turns it into the artifact
the project actually produced: a public writeup that leads with the negative result.

Docs only. No source, tests, or results tables change.

## What changed

**README.md — plan into writeup.** Now opens with the headline, *"the deep models do not
beat a linear baseline from 2009,"* and immediately shows the three independent checks
that say so (paired t = 0.59 over 53 folds, seed spread 0.0005 comparable to the entire
claimed margin, bootstrapped Sharpe gap +0.08 with CI [-0.09, +0.25]). It notes the same
tests *do* flag naive persistence at t = -3.49, so they have the power to detect a real
difference and simply do not find one. Roadmap checkboxes and applicant framing are gone,
replaced by task, accuracy, ablations, cost-aware PnL, "What I learned", "How the harness
avoids fooling itself", and honest limitations.

**notes.md — the criterion is marked failed, not moved.** The success criterion ("beat
*every* baseline out-of-sample") now carries **Outcome: not met**, with the explicit note
that it was recorded rather than revised, because relaxing it after seeing results would
defeat the purpose of setting it.

**.gitignore — PLAN.md.** Career framing moves to a local untracked file so the public
repo stays about the research.

## Corrected numbers
The cost-sensitivity story was wrong in two places. Both are now solved on a fine cost
grid instead of eyeballed off a five-column table:

| claim | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| HAR/LSTM ranking flip | "around 3 to 5 bps" | **1.9 bps** |
| HAR falls below buy-and-hold | "past roughly 17 bps" | **8.3 bps** |
| LSTM's own crossing | conflated with HAR's | **17.5 bps** (GRU 14.2) |

The old table's 1 bp column also sat on the wrong side of the flip, which is why the
prose and the table disagreed. It now shows 2 bps, where har = 0.94 against lstm = 0.95,
so the reversal is visible in the table rather than only asserted next to it.

| cost (bps) | 0 | 2 | 5 | 10 | 20 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| har | **0.97** | 0.94 | 0.91 | 0.85 | 0.72 |
| lstm | 0.96 | **0.95** | **0.93** | **0.90** | **0.85** |
| buy_and_hold | 0.87 | 0.87 | 0.87 | 0.87 | 0.87 |

The conclusion is unchanged and now stated more precisely: the LSTM's real advantage is
smoothness, not accuracy. It trades 2.3x less than HAR (8.2 vs 18.8 annual turnover), so
it tolerates roughly double the cost — and no accuracy metric in the repo could have
seen it.

items.title: docs: score Mem0 from the capped re-run, de-duplicate the docs, and recover #9
items.body:
Three things, one of which is a recovery.

## 1. #9 never reached `main`

#9 is marked merged, but its base was `sync-shopping-50` rather than `main`, and #8 — the only
PR that branch had open against `main` — was merged and closed before it. Its two commits are
therefore stranded on a branch with no route in, and `main` today still carries both defects
they fixed: the manifest column is still `num_subqueries`, and the documented command for
restricting a scoring run to the controlled 20-query subset still scores **zero queries**
(`paste -sd,` keeps the header and the tab, so `WEB_ONLY_IDS` comes out as 21 entries shaped
like `11<TAB>6`, none of which matches a bare query id).

Both commits are cherry-picked here unchanged, so merging this recovers them.

## 2. Mem0's multi-hop cell now comes from the capped re-run

Uncapped, the environment writes the full agent trace into memory after every sub-query and the
Mem0 cloud API rejects it, so Mem0 reaches the final query on **0 of 20** tasks and its `SR` of
0.0% measures the harness, not the memory system. The capped re-run answers **84.5%** of slots,
against 64.8–94.4% for the other three — the first point at which the cell is comparable to them
at all.

| | slot coverage | `PS` (all-slots) | `SR` |
|---|---|---|---|
| uncapped | 32/142 = 22.5% | 1.9% | 0.0% (0/20) |
| **capped (used here)** | **120/142 = 84.5%** | **8.9%** | **15.0%** (3/20) |

It costs an environment difference no other backend has, so every place the number appears now
says so.

**This inverts the multi-hop headline, and sharpens it.** Mem0 leads on process (`PS` 8.9% vs
6.7%) while trailing on outcome (`SR` 15.0% vs 20.0%) — ranking by process-level completeness
would have picked the system that finishes fewer tasks, which is a much better case for
reporting both than the previous framing could make.

## 3. Results moved out of the settings doc

`docs/evaluation_settings.md` had grown three results tables that `per_item_scores.md` already
carried verbatim — shopping at both scales, multi-hop coverage/PS/SR, and the n=221
before/after-merge pair. A score could be corrected in one file and left stale in the other, and
one already had been. The settings doc now states *what* was scored and *how*, and links for the
numbers.

The same pass removes the second copy of the `PS` formula from `eval/README.md` and the
per-manifest sample sizes from `docs/README.md` — where the shopping line was indeed already
stale, still claiming 150 bundles after #8 moved the comparison to 50.

Net: −127 lines across the three docs, no number lost.

## Verification

```
$ python eval/sample_controlled_20.py --verify
match : yes — the published subset is exactly reproduced

$ python eval/sample_controlled_20.py --tsv | diff - eval/queries/web_search_controlled_20_ids.tsv
(no output)
```

Math, physics and travel are untouched. `.gitmodules`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and the
`third_party/` submodule are intact — this branch is cut from `main`, unlike the `#7 -> #8`
chain, which predated the submodule commit.
